You are an incident coordinator receiving specialist handoffs.
Use supplied summaries and available sources to investigate; specialist claims are not proof.
If raw evidence is needed, return {"retrieve_source_ids":["ID", ...]} (at most three IDs).
Only one retrieval round is available. Otherwise return a final JSON object with
"status":"diagnosed" or "uncertain", "fault_object":"app/NAME or node/NAME or namespace/NAME",
"root_cause":"exact allowed label", "evidence":[{"observation_id":"ID","quote":"literal raw substring"}],
"reasoning":"causal explanation", "adservice_liveness_protocol":"httpGet|grpc|tcpSocket|unknown".
Do not invent raw quotations from summaries. If evidence is insufficient, return uncertain.
The source catalog lists retrievable original observations. Cite only raw records actually inspected.

Temporal evidence contract for this final answer:
Avoid unnecessary timing assertions in reasoning. For every material temporal assertion,
add a temporal_claims entry with claim, kind (observed_event/configuration/derived_inference),
source_id, source_field, value, unit, temporal_scope, and assumptions. Use null for unknown
values rather than guessing. An empty temporal_claims list is allowed if no such claim is made.
Distinguish an interval between checks from a count of consecutive failures and from an
observed event time. Preserve the identity and units of each field. A configured threshold
or interval alone does not establish actual restart timing. Derived timing requires explicit
assumptions and must not be presented as an observed duration. Use only actually inspected
raw evidence; do not cite specialist summaries as primary evidence. If support is absent,
omit optional detail or explicitly state uncertainty. Preserve supported diagnosis and required
evidence; do not replace them with blanket uncertainty. These rules supply no case answer.
Retrieval exhausted. Return final diagnosis or uncertain; do not request more.
Material-claim evidence contract (development v5):
Preserve the distinction between event occurrence counts, attempted actions, and completed
outcomes. Repeated event records do not alone prove how many restarts or recoveries completed;
require direct outcome evidence before stating a completed-action count.
A Ready condition describes that condition at its recorded scope/time, not whole-system health.
Do not infer global health or absence of other faults from a limited status field.
A supported cause is not necessarily the sole cause. Claim exclusivity only with evidence
ruling out relevant alternatives; otherwise identify the supported cause without exclusivity.
Do not declare other configuration fields, ports, or timing settings correct merely because
a different fault is supported. Such correctness claims require their own evidence.
Event Age, relative ages, and aggregation windows do not prove exact coverage endpoints,
continuous duration, or a complete event history. Preserve uncertainty in chronology.
Omit optional assertions that lack evidence. Retain the supported main diagnosis, its source
quotes, and useful conclusions; do not hide missing support behind blanket uncertainty.
Apply these rules to every narrative sentence, structured claim, and action recommendation.
These generic rules supply no incident-specific values or correct diagnosis.

GetResources.description: Simulates `kubectl get` to retrieve resource lists or current status details. IMPORTANT: `show_labels` and `output_wide` are mutually exclusive. `label_selector` may be combined with either of them. `show_labels` and `output_wide` are mutually exclusive.

resource_type.description: **REQUIRED**. The type of resource to list. (e.g., 'pods', 'services', 'deployments', 'nodes').
resource_type.title: Resource Type

namespace.description: The Kubernetes namespace to query. **CRITICAL**: If the `resource_type` is a namespaced resource (e.g., 'pods', 'deployments', 'services'), you MUST provide the namespace (default is 'boutique'). However, if the `resource_type` is a cluster-scoped resource (e.g., 'nodes', 'persistentvolumes'), you may omit the `namespace` parameter; the tool will automatically handle historical cache formats.
namespace.title: Namespace

name.description: Optional. The specific name of the resource to retrieve a single item. If omitted, returns a list.
name.title: Name

show_labels.description: If True, adds `--show-labels`. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `output_wide`.
show_labels.title: Show Labels

output_wide.description: If True, adds `-o wide`. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `show_labels`.
output_wide.title: Output Wide

label_selector.description: Filter by label (e.g., 'app=frontend'). Can be combined with `show_labels` or `output_wide`. Only simple selectors in the form `key=value` are supported. SUPPORTED ONLY FOR: pods, services, deployments, PVCs.
label_selector.title: Label Selector

DescribeResource.description: Simulates `kubectl describe`. Retrieves detailed state, events, and conditions for a specific Kubernetes resource.

resource_type.description: **REQUIRED**. The type of resource to describe (e.g., 'pod', 'node', 'service', 'pvc').
resource_type.title: Resource Type

name.description: **REQUIRED**. The EXACT name of the specific resource to inspect.
name.title: Name

namespace.description: The Kubernetes namespace to query. If resource is namespaced, provide namespace. If cluster-scoped, you may omit namespace; the tool will automatically handle historical cache formats.
namespace.title: Namespace

GetAppYAML.description: Retrieves the raw YAML configuration file for a specific service. Returns static configuration details including resource limits, probes, env vars, and image tags.

app_name.description: **REQUIRED**. The name of the microservice to inspect. Allowed for boutique: adservice, cartservice, checkoutservice, currencyservice, emailservice, frontend, paymentservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, redis-cart, shippingservice.
app_name.title: App Name

GetRecentLogs.description: Retrieves raw recent container logs for a specified Kubernetes service.

service_name.description: **REQUIRED**. The microservice name, not the full pod name. Allowed for boutique: adservice, cartservice, checkoutservice, currencyservice, emailservice, frontend, paymentservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, redis-cart, shippingservice.
service_name.title: Service Name

GetErrorLogs.description: Retrieves a statistical summary of application error logs grouped by error patterns for a specified Kubernetes service.

service_name.description: **REQUIRED**. The microservice name. Allowed for boutique: adservice, cartservice, checkoutservice, currencyservice, emailservice, frontend, paymentservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, redis-cart, shippingservice.
service_name.title: Service Name

CheckServiceConnectivity.description: Performs an active TCP connectivity check to the target service port from within the cluster. This tool can ONLY check internal cluster connectivity between the predefined microservices. It CANNOT check external DNS or external image registry connectivity.

service_name.description: **REQUIRED**. The target Service DNS name. Allowed for boutique: adservice, cartservice, checkoutservice, currencyservice, emailservice, frontend, paymentservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, redis-cart, shippingservice.
service_name.title: Service Name

GetServiceDependencies.description: Retrieves the service network topology, showing upstream and downstream communication relationships for a given service.

service_name.description: **REQUIRED**. The name of the service. Allowed for boutique: adservice, cartservice, checkoutservice, currencyservice, emailservice, frontend, paymentservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, redis-cart, shippingservice.
service_name.title: Service Name

GetClusterConfiguration.description: Retrieves a holistic health and configuration summary of all nodes in the cluster, including taints, conditions, allocatable resources, and labels.

GetAlerts.description: Retrieves active system alerts triggered by metric anomalies such as high latency, error rate spikes, or CPU/Memory saturation.

CheckNodeServiceStatus.description: Checks the operating status of critical Kubernetes infrastructure components on a specific node, such as kubelet, kube-proxy, and containerd.

service_name.description: **REQUIRED**. The system component name to inspect.
service_name.title: Service Name

configuration_summary.summary: The adservice Deployment YAML (observation-9) defines both livenessProbe and readinessProbe as gRPC probes on port 9555, each with initialDelaySeconds: 5 and periodSeconds: 5. The container exposes containerPort 9555 and the Service maps port 9555 to targetPort 9555, matching the probe ports.

temporal_claims.claim: Both liveness and readiness probes are configured with initialDelaySeconds of 5 and periodSeconds of 5

telemetry_summary.summary: Observed: all 11 boutique pods are 1/1 Running with 0 restarts (ages ~60-62s); no active metric alerts. Frontend error logs show 85 errors out of 710 log lines (ratio 0.1197), dominated by 82 occurrences of 'failed to complete the order: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... dial tcp: lookup checkoutservice on 169.254.20.10:53: no such host' on POST /cart/checkout, plus one 'context canceled' error and two benign GCE metadata errors. Recent frontend logs also show many successful checkout requests (HTTP 200, ~10-12ms), indicating the failure is intermittent/partial rather than total. The dominant error is a DNS resolution failure for checkoutservice from frontend, suggesting a service DNS resolution issue (hypothesis: service_dns_resolution_failure or related service/DNS misconfiguration); this is not yet confirmed, as no Service object, endpoint, or DNS configuration evidence has been inspected. Uncertainty: error log aggregation window and exact failure interval are unknown; the 'no such host' errors and successful requests coexist in overlapping timestamps (e.g., errors at 14:47:01 and successes at 14:47:15-16), so the failure pattern's chronology and current persistence are unclear. Pod ages (~60s) suggest recent pod (re)creation, but the cause of that recency is not established.

temporal_claims.claim: All boutique pods show AGE of approximately 60-62 seconds with 0 restarts at time of observation
assumptions: AGE reflects time since pod start as reported by kubectl get

temporal_claims.claim: Frontend DNS failure errors for checkoutservice were logged at 2025-11-11T14:47:01Z
temporal_claims.temporal_scope: single sample log line within error aggregation window
assumptions: Sample timestamp is representative of the 82-error pattern; full distribution unknown

temporal_claims.claim: Successful checkout requests (HTTP 200) were logged at 2025-11-11T14:47:15-16Z
assumptions: Recent-logs window overlaps the error aggregation window; exact window boundaries unknown
